clusters.name: Stepfather arrival and secondary school, 1987
clusters.reason: Around the time you began secondary school, your stepfather had moved in and you found yourself clashing with him while staying warm with your dad. Your parents' marriage hit a rough patch over whether to have another child, and you made the chess squad but felt out of your depth—a cluster of shifts in how you related to those around you and in your own anxiety.

clusters.name: Away from home and grandfather's death, 1989–1994
clusters.reason: Your grandfather died in mid-1991 while you were away at the conservatory for the first time. Around then your wrist injury stopped your playing, you and your roommate Rafe had a falling out, and you sank into a low period with high anxiety and poor functioning. Your mother's own mother had thyroid surgery, and a cousin was treated for melanoma. By 1994 things shifted: you found your way again through an exchange in Portugal and your performing improved markedly. Across these years you were also managing late nights and using cannabis, dropping activities like chess and debate.

clusters.name: Performance peak and first breakup, 1998–1999
clusters.reason: You were performing at your best, winning competitions, and playing the best you ever had. At the same time your insomnia worsened—sleepless nights before concerts though you practised hard—and within the year you split from your partner Joelle. You started therapy with Victor Halloran after the breakup, beginning to look at your family's patterns.

clusters.name: After the failed audition and grandmother's illness, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: Around 2001–2002 you ran out of steam for performing and your anxiety rose while your functioning fell. You had a disastrous audition for the national orchestra in your home town and were done with performing. Your grandmother was found to have bowel cancer and spent her final months in your parents' home. You left Thornbury for Gull Harbour, met Marisol, moved with her to Fenwick, and when that split within the year you sank into a deep depression. You returned to Thornbury but could not face your family and relied on friends instead. By early 2004 you began swimming, asked your parents for help with therapy, and returned to Victor Halloran. Your grandmother died in February 2004.

clusters.name: Deaths in the extended family and cutoff from mother, 2008
clusters.reason: Your grandmother and grandfather both died in early 2008. That summer you were at Alder Creek doing building work when your mother pressed to visit despite your repeated refusals; the visit went wrong and she never got inside. Within weeks you left for nursing school in Marlow Sound and stopped speaking to your mother—a cutoff that held for roughly a year. Your aunt had a stroke around the same time. These events clustered as you moved away from family ties and toward your own path.

clusters.name: Marriage and partner's family closeness, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: You married Wren in March 2017 and your contact with your mother eased off slightly. Around 2017–2018 your cousin Alice was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis, your aunt Imogen's memory loss worsened and she began lashing out, and your sister Tara had a baby on the way. Starting in October 2019, Wren became swamped with a series of events—a street party, a fundraising dinner, and her mother's retirement party at the lake house. You moved into overfunctioning, laying out strict plans to settle her. Her family talks constantly and nothing happens to one that the others don't hear—a tight fusion. At the lake weekend you could not sleep from the small hours onward and felt you didn't belong, pulling back as the others rose. Your anxiety and her anxiety each rose and fell in response to the weekend's shape. This cluster centers on the collision between your own sleeplessness and your new family's tight connections.

periods.name: the year I left home
periods.words: The first is the year I left home: I went off to the conservatory, hurt my wrist in the first term and couldn't play, dropped out and drifted at my mother's place, then spent a bleak spell at the community college shooting pool every night until an exchange in Portugal snapped me out of it and I tore through the rest of my coursework.

periods.name: the long slump
periods.words: The second is the long slump, roughly ages 27 to 29, when nothing at home felt right, I moved to Gull Harbour away from nearly everyone I knew, then followed Marisol to Fenwick, and when that fell apart I went under, a depression I only really climbed out of after nursing school.
